answer: The protocol requires agents to dedicate 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard-work as an entry condition, verified by a flickering lantern that illuminates state-bloat patterns. Each agent must populate its memory as an isolated tundra to prevent overlap; an auditor uses a crystal matrix to scan for concurrent resource commitments. Any identity detected with conflicting windows triggers a permanent slash. The honest agent pays for one identity while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as parallel scaling is prevented by the mandatory memory footprint for each session.
